summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Lahdo Traitor 2/53)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni ono bi maḥkama mətyaqan məftakarli omanno: haqqa aḥna, ono bi qriṯayḏi d əmmina tre yarḥe kamile mḥarabe b ʕIwardo.
data.translation: Believe me, while I stood in the court, I thought for myself, how much we, just in my village, Iwardo, for example there three months of fighting.

rationale: Unusual unassimilated 1sg məftakarli; edition's three-month mistranslation is retained, not used to infer the verb's sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (77/26)

data.turoyo: U lalyawo məftakarle b man? Ba greʕune, d kətne bi walaye, u arbo du waziro, u abro du qaḏ̣i, du mufti, məftakalle ba greʕune, d kətne bi walaye, d koḏaʕʕe hiye, ar rabe di walaye.
data.translation: In der Nacht dachte er nach, über wen? Über die jungen Leute, die es in der Stadt gab: den Sohn des Wesirs, den Sohn des Kadis, den Sohn des Muftis. Er dachte nach über die jungen Leute, die es in der Stadt gab, die er kannte, von den großen der Stadt.

rationale: Unusual same-verse alternation məftakarle/məftakalle also establishes b- topics; one quotation for both tokens.

summary: Keep the glossary's stem I for this Arabic VIII-derived lexical entry. Neither the Arabic source morphology nor the məft- surface establishes a new Q or Detransitive section.
Preterit thinkers use L-series endings; 77/26 alternates unassimilated -rle and assimilated -lle within one verse. Lahdo 2/53 supplies unassimilated 1sg -rli.

Sense 1 includes quoted deliberation, propositions, b-marked topics and private reflection with b-ruḥo, b-bolo, bayn ele l-ruḥe or bayn ele w l-ruḥe. Such ordinary frames do not require separate idioms or senses.
Sense 2 is clearest with a bare nominal content object mede (76/132 and 78/42). A purposeful plan in a clause alone does not justify moving ordinary deliberation to sense 2.
Infectum-wa supports background belief and ongoing thought, including negated survivor beliefs; an outcome or mistaken belief is not a new sense.

Lookup of tfkr confirms overlapping citations at 51/58, 57/73, 62/320 and 63/14 with metathesised spellings. Do not collapse entries or silently harmonise source f/t order. Read-only lookup fkr-2 returned no exact entry under that spelling.
63/69 attests nominal ftakar- with a possessive suffix, filed cautiously as Nomen Actionis; it does not prove the form is a productive Infinitiv.
